name: Russian nationalism
summary: Russian nationalism in its dominant contemporary form is a state-centred, imperial-minded nationalism that treats Russia as a distinct Orthodox-Slavic civilization with a great-power mission. It pairs strong executive rule, military strength and sovereignty against the West with traditional family values, and sees Russians, Ukrainians and Belarusians as one people. Official versions call Russia multiethnic with Russians as the state-forming nation, while ethnic ultranationalists want a narrower Russia for Russians.
scope: The mainstream state-nationalist (derzhavnyi) strand of the Putin era, based on Putin's 2021 essay on the unity of Russians and Ukrainians, the Russian world concept and the traditional-values agenda, with Slavophile, Orthodox and Eurasianist ideas as background. It excludes the neo-Nazi and neo-pagan fringe, the liberal-civic Westernizer strand and Soviet-era internationalism, and it does not represent Navalny-style ethnic nationalism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a nationalist theme; inferred from the Soviet-era legacy of state-funded care and a state-centred view of the nation's welfare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Sources give no nationalist line on wage floors, and adherents split between paternalist state-capitalists and market-leaning conservatives.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty and state-centred framing; the state is expected to steer strategic sectors rather than leave them to the market.

public-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the statist, great-power tradition (imperial and Soviet) in which strategic industries serve the state's strength.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Nationalist currents are split between anti-oligarch populism and loyalty to a propertied elite; the sources do not settle it.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not a defining issue; the national-unity ideal sits uneasily with both union independence and its suppression.

property-fundamental.rationale: The essay condemns oligarchic plunder in Ukraine, but there is no stated nationalist doctrine on property rights, so adherents are split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Criticism of oligarchs exists, but there is no stated programme; the state-first view cuts both ways.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on family, collectivism and population strength, which sits poorly with dismantling social support.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective ownership by workers is a left-wing aim, not a nationalist one; inferred from the statist and anti-Bolshevik stance.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security and order are prized above individual liberty; the 'agents of chaos' framing of opponents makes surveillance easy to justify.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Traditional-values conservatism treats drug legalization as part of Western moral decay; inferred, not directly sourced.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Official Russian nationalism uses extremism laws and curbs radical nationalists, so restriction is tolerated, though adherents differ on its targets.

strong-leader.rationale: Imperial and Putin-era strands centre on autocratic or strongman rule, with 'managed democracy' as the model.

state-harmful.rationale: Every major strand treats a strong state as the guardian of the nation; anarchism is alien to it.

limit-guns.rationale: Not an issue in the sources; inferred from the state-order orientation and the existing restrictive regime.

empower-police-military.rationale: Great-power status and internal order rest on strong security organs in imperial and post-2014 nationalism.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the traditional-values agenda, which opposes permissive sexual morality.

decide-locally.rationale: The imperial and state strands favour a centralised unitary state, and the 2020-era state treats regional separateness warily.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the order-and-authority outlook favouring firm punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: Traditional family values are a core theme of the regime's conservative-nationalist ideology.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Hostility to sexual minorities and the portrayal of Western tolerance as moral collapse are central to the values agenda.

abortion-legal.rationale: Orthodox-traditionalist and pronatalist currents oppose abortion, though it remains legal in Russia and adherents differ.

more-religion-public.rationale: Orthodoxy is one leg of the Orthodoxy-Autocracy-Nationality tradition and is central to Slavophile and modern strands, though neo-pagan wings dissent.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Western race-focused redress is cast as liberal ideology imposed from outside; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The values agenda treats gender as natural and rejects Western gender theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Preserving Russian culture, language and tradition is the defining aim of the ideology.

gradual-change.rationale: Conservative at home and hostile to revolution, but revisionist abroad, so only a weak agreement.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Anti-migrant sentiment ('Russia for Russians') runs through post-Soviet nationalism, though the state keeps labour migration from Central Asia.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sovereignty is understood as spiritual and national self-determination, and the 'liberal international order' is rejected.

free-trade.rationale: Inferred from sovereignty and anti-Western hostility; mainstream adherents favour protection of strategic autonomy.

nation-first.rationale: The nationally oriented, sovereign state is placed ahead of 'abstract transnational' arrangements.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The West's rights-based interventions are cast as hypocritical liberal projects, so adherents reject them.

open-borders.rationale: Borders and the national community are central, and anti-migrant nationalism is explicit in the ultranationalist wing.

limit-growth.rationale: Great-power ambition rests on economic and military strength; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not a nationalist theme; inferred from hydrocarbon-based state power and scepticism of Western agendas.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources are silent; strands range from Soviet technological pride to Orthodox scepticism of modernity.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from Russia's nuclear industry and its role in great-power standing.

revolution-justified.rationale: Opponents are cast as 'agents of chaos' and revolution is the Bolshevik rupture the essay blames for Russia's losses.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not addressed; adherents favour rule by the leader and state rather than either experts or the public.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred from rejection of Bolshevism, though Soviet nostalgia gives some support.

socialized-markets.rationale: A left-economic model not tied to nationalism; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; no nationalist tradition of such a tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Family continuity is valued, so heavy inheritance taxes are unlikely; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from paternalist, work-and-family-oriented statism.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from the stress on sovereignty and strategic independence.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from the statist, great-power orientation toward strategic sectors.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The tradition has peasant-commune and large-estate strands; no clear line.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A Marxist aim at odds with a nation-state ideology.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from statism; an anarcho-capitalist idea that is foreign to the tradition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Imperial organic and national-bolshevik currents might favour it, but mainstream sources do not address it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Putin-era rule is built on a dominant party in a 'managed democracy', not formal single-party rule; Soviet-nostalgic wings differ.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The imperial strand is loyal to the Romanovs and neo-monarchists exist, but the Putin-era mainstream is republican in form.

democracy-best.rationale: 'Sovereign democracy' and the framing of dissent as extremism show a reserved attitude toward liberal democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Plebiscites are used for legitimation but are not a stated nationalist principle.

workers-councils.rationale: Soviet-style council power is a Bolshevik institution that nationalists reject.

right-to-secede.rationale: The essay stresses historical territorial unity and conditions on independence, and the state treats secession as an existential threat.

natural-rulers.rationale: Autocratic and elitist traditions imply a ruling stratum; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: The tradition (Black Hundreds, radical nationalism, war-readiness) accepts force; the state monopolises it.

war-builds-character.rationale: Commentators describe a cult of war in Russian-world discourse, but this is not stated as a doctrine.

separate-church-state.rationale: Orthodoxy is fused with state and nation in the imperial, Slavophile and Putin-era traditions.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Orthodoxy shapes public morality but the tradition does not call for scripture-based law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state's monopoly on force and defense is essential to nationalist statism.

military-superiority.rationale: Great-power status (derzhava) depends on military strength, central across strands.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Putin-era nationalism calls Russia multiethnic with Russians as the 'state-forming nation'; only ethnic ultranationalists want a single-ethnicity state.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nation and civilization, not class, drive history in every nationalist strand.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred from hierarchical, conservative outlook and anti-Bolshevik stance.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a unitary state that keeps authority over all territory.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from imperial self-understanding and from rejecting Western moral claims.

civilizational-union.rationale: The Russian world and Eurasian civilization concepts call for a union of peoples sharing Orthodoxy, language and history.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Collectivism and duty are emphasised over individual self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Collectivism, patriotism and duty to community are listed as core themes of the values agenda.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not a defined position; Slavophile romanticism and instrumental state views coexist.

limit-population.rationale: Pronatalism and family values make population limits unwelcome; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Great-power aims rest on industry; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Conservatism favours stability and tradition over disruptive speed; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from Orthodox and traditional-values suspicion of Western modernity.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from personal, leader-centred rule.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the security-state stance and the 'agents of chaos' view of opponents.

restore-past-order.rationale: Revanchist aims to restore Soviet or imperial influence suggest yes, but the ideology is also modernising.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pragmatism marks the state but ideology (values, sovereignty) is also loud.

direct-action.rationale: Order-first state nationalism distrusts street politics, and challengers are called extremists.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A great-power, industrial-state ideology rejects primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A Marxist utopian aim wholly foreign to nationalism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist principle; inferred rejection, though Soviet nostalgia tempers it.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Marxist theory of exploitation is rejected by nationalism as class-based doctrine.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A Bolshevik doctrine that the essay blames for Russia's losses.

collective-farming.rationale: Tied to Soviet policy; Putin-era nationalists criticise Bolshevik collectivisation, though nostalgia exists.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Leninist thesis; nationalists blame Western geopolitics and not capitalism as such.

taxation-theft.rationale: A libertarian view at odds with state-centred nationalism.

harm-principle.rationale: The traditional-values agenda restricts conduct on moral grounds beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Community, nation and duty take precedence over individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Mass conscription belongs to the great-power tradition and is retained in modern Russia.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Loyalty to the state and nation is the opposite of an exit-based view.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is a sacral and national entity, not a firm; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Hostility to liberal intellectuals and Western media exists, but the claim of their dominance over elected officials is not a Russian nationalist theme.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Official nationalism is multiethnic and avoids race science, though some ultranationalist wings differ.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; some imperial and neo-monarchist currents favour estates, but not the mainstream.

total-state.rationale: Statist and authoritarian but not totalitarian in doctrine; Eurasianist radicals differ.

national-rebirth.rationale: Putin-era nationalism presents recovery from 1990s weakness as national revival and is mixed with cultural-moral renewal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Russian world doctrine is described as revanchist and neo-imperial, and the 2021 essay warns Moscow will defend 'historical territories'.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Loyalty to the tsar was imperial doctrine, but feudal oaths between lords are not a nationalist position.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is not defended by modern nationalism; Westernizers and Slavophiles alike opposed it.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Mainly a Western postmodern thesis, though the regime treats history as a battlefield; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: The Russian way is presented as a civilizational alternative to a 'hypocritical' liberal universalism.

single-common-good.rationale: Collectivist and Orthodox traditions favour a unified national good over interest-group balancing.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not a nationalist concern; positions range widely among strands.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Support for compatriots abroad and the 'Russian world' implies a welcome for co-nationals; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Russian is already dominant and promoted; the question is mainly about other languages, so adherents are not engaged.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchical, statist outlook.

school-vouchers.rationale: The sources give no nationalist line on school funding, and adherents have no shared position.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty and stability emphasis; fiscal conservatism accompanies Putin-era policy.

economic-freedom.rationale: Political order is prized over liberal economic freedom, and the connection to political freedom is not accepted.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; imperial tradition favours both moral example and sacred authority.

national-self-determination.rationale: The essay accepts a people's self-determination in principle but denies Ukrainians a separate nation and attaches conditions, so the position is split.

force-without-un.rationale: The state defends a sovereign right to act abroad, as with Crimea and Ukraine, without Security Council approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Orthodoxy and tradition are valued over Enlightenment rationalism; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from nation-first and anti-migrant views.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from collectivist duty and traditional work ethic.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalism subordinates class divisions to national unity in all strands.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving tradition and heritage is core to the conservative-nationalist agenda.

dominated-front.rationale: Russian world and Eurasianist doctrine promote a front against Western dominance and Pax Americana.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred from nationalism's rejection of proletarian internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Traditional-values doctrine assumes complementary roles for men and women.

ban-interest.rationale: Not a feature of Russian nationalism.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Official nationalism is multiethnic, and racial segregation is not part of any mainstream strand.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist thesis; nationalists see the state as embodying the nation.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from the importance of hydrocarbons to state power.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Imperial and integral nationalism sought assimilation into Russian culture, and post-Soviet nationalists demand the same of migrants.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement theory is a Western far-right idea; some radicals voice similar fears, but it is not mainstream.

national-mission.rationale: Russian messianism and the civilizational mission are recurring themes, from Slavophiles to Eurasianists.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The values agenda rejects Western feminist critique of gender order.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nationalists denounce oligarchs and foreign-backed elites, but the regime itself rejects the charge, so adherents split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not a Russian nationalist theme; Orthodox and pronatalist values oppose it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The state's reframing of Soviet and tsarist history and defence of its security organs reject such accountability.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The nationalist state is expansive in culture, security and economy.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Official nationalism is multiethnic and Russian identity has long absorbed intermarriage, though ultranationalist fringes differ.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Formally the essay affirms respect for Ukrainians as people, but the ideology also ranks nations and values, so only a weak yes.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with little bearing on nationalism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Russian imperial expansion was itself settlement, and adherents reject the colonial label.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; unified law fits the centralist ideal but the state tolerates exceptions in regions.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Orthodoxy's privileged status in the tradition implies limits on proselytising; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Orthodox tradition and post-Soviet revival favour religious culture teaching in school; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The 'anti-Russia' framing treats the state as under external threat that justifies strength, though not in socialist terms.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The sovereign-democracy idea invokes popular will while the leader embodies it; adherents split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred from an export-oriented resource economy and the sovereignty emphasis.

population-transfer.rationale: Official nationalism declares itself multiethnic, though Soviet deportations and ultranationalist wings differ.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The state justified force over Ukraine and Crimea as defending historical and national interests, so absolute non-aggression is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Strands include geopolitical struggle ideas but no stated doctrine.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The state bans groups such as Russian National Unity and treats opponents as extremists.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican theory not engaged in the sources.

separated-powers.rationale: The tradition prefers a unified authority, as in managed democracy.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine rejected by nationalism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not addressed; Orthodox charity and nationalist statism have no stated doctrine on this.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy that Russian nationalism never addresses, with no basis for inferring a side.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the order-first state and anti-disorder outlook.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Pronatalism implies population is a strength, not the cause of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ethnic ultranationalists say yes, while official Putin-era nationalism praises multiethnic harmony; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contrary to hierarchical, leader-centred authority; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Opponents are cast as extremists or agents of chaos, and a security-first state accepts emergency powers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from a paternalist state tradition.

party-controls-media.rationale: The regime restricts and steers media; inferred, though not as a doctrine of party control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not a nationalist principle; the army serves the state and head of state.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from anti-migrant and assimilationist outlook.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A Bolshevik-style egalitarian measure; inferred rejection.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party organisation is not a nationalist doctrine, and Putin-era party politics gives no clear rule.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sovereignty is a core value, and the EU model is part of the rejected liberal order.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The presidential-autocratic tradition places command in the head of state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Russian Orthodox Church is episcopal and the Russian world concept builds on it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Orthodoxy is allied with the state but under it, not ruling it.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism was Lenin's policy and is the opposite of patriotic loyalty.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The values agenda supports limiting content seen as morally corrupting; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The managed-democracy model favours strong, continuing leadership; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Not a feature of the managed-democracy model.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Russia keeps its own alliances such as the CSTO; the ideology rejects Western alliances, not alliances in general.

people-in-arms.rationale: Professional and conscript state forces are favoured over popular militias.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Slavophile romanticism of the village and tradition supports a mild yes.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The essay presents Russians, Ukrainians and Belarusians as one people divided by Bolshevik-drawn borders and questions the post-Soviet settlement.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectual and anti-liberal rhetoric exists, but it is not a stated tenet.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Civilizational thinking says cultures are different, but the ideology also claims moral superiority over a decadent West.

death-penalty.rationale: Nationalists usually support it, although Russia keeps a moratorium; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality and sexuality education are part of the Western agenda the values doctrine rejects.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Orthodox culture teaching exists, but creationism is not a core demand.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Traditional-values doctrine supports moral regulation; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Russian world concept stresses ties of descent and culture beyond the territory.

minority-language-support.rationale: Assimilationist strands prefer Russian dominance, while the state tolerates some minority languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from a unified-law, Orthodox-dominant view.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity to tradition and collective norms is valued over individuality.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The essay stresses sovereignty vs foreign control, but not property-system change.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The state-centred view prefers continuity and top-down constitutional change.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The values-based, order-first regime accepts curbs on freedoms for stability and strength.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from nation-first stance and rejection of universalist moral duties.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Russia's nuclear arsenal underpins great-power status and the 'Nuclear Orthodoxy' theme.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: A popularly legitimated strong president fits the current model; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The essay warns Moscow will defend its 'historical territories' and treats Crimea as a settled historic choice.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The collectivist, duty-first outlook subordinates property to national interest.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet period is mixed in nationalist memory, with Stalinist pride; the thesis is a left-communist one.

collective-defense.rationale: Allied defense fits the CSTO, though the ideology targets NATO.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The essay and OSW frame Crimea's accession as its 'historic choice', so adherents reject the occupation label.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Orthodox Church is respected and allied with the state in the nationalist tradition.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Strongman presidents are shown above party competition; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The essay and strong-state ideology treat separatism as a threat to be countered, even by force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Centralist; the unitary-state ideal leaves little room for regions with separate systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The imperial strand treated the tsar as anointed, but this is not claimed for modern rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Russia has a flat income tax and the statist right accepts it; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Autocratic tradition tolerates it in practice, but modern nationalists state allegiance to law.

space-expansion.rationale: The Cosmist and Soviet technological pride are mentioned in nationalist imaginaries; weak inference.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; autocratic and Westernizer strands diverge.

leader-cult.rationale: Commentators describe a personalised leader image in the regime; adherents accept it, but it is not stated doctrine.

equal-parenting.rationale: Traditional-family doctrine assigns distinct parenting roles; inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist thesis foreign to Russian nationalism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Redistribution is a Bolshevik/populist programme that nationalists reject.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources do not address refugee return, and inferences from Russian compatriot policy point both ways.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Russian world doctrine and 2021 essay justify influence and claims over areas inhabited by Russians and Russian speakers.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Orthodox tradition does not punish leaving the faith by law.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not a Russian Orthodox demand; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Sovereignty is a core value, though Eurasian integration includes economic union; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The All-Russian nation concept and Pan-Slavism call for unity of East Slavs across borders.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; the imperial and Soviet systems varied.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Compatriot policy supports protecting kin abroad, but emigration is not discussed as an alternative.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist thesis; nationalism stresses nation, spirit and culture.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not addressed by the sources, and state-capitalist tendencies point both ways.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from the state-capitalist leaning that supports rescuing strategic firms.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Hostility to liberal institutional checks and the idea of an embodied national will supports it.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from rejection of Western gender-equality agendas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Sovereignty is stressed but closed autarky with colonies is not a Russian nationalist model.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet nostalgia versus market realities.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The regime paints revolutionary movements as agents of chaos.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The imperial strand favours hereditary monarchy while modern nationalism does not take a stand.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The state-nationalist line treats Russia as a distinct civilization whose history should be taught as the central narrative.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Imperial Russian tradition justified rule over other peoples as a civilizing mission, but modern doctrine frames influence as protecting compatriots; inferred from that.

patriotic-education.rationale: The values-based legitimation of the Putin era lists patriotism among core traditional values to be instilled.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not a Russian issue; inferred from the rejection of Western identity politics and traditional-values stance.

public-money-creation.rationale: Nationalists criticise dollar dominance but adherents split between state-centred paternalists and market-leaning technocrats.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The doctrine casts the West as in civilizational decline, so inferred sympathy for a collapse thesis; economics itself was not addressed.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The Russian world doctrine and Putin's essay seek Russian political and cultural influence over former Soviet and imperial lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: Official nationalism favours sovereign integration through BRICS and import substitution rather than delinking; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The thesis comes from Leninist internationalism, which state nationalism opposes in favour of national solidarity; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The state-centred, paternalist model does not defend broad private freedom of association; inferred from that.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: State sovereignty and strong executive rule are central, and rights are subordinated to state interest; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Putin's essay presents Soviet-drawn borders as arbitrary, so inferred sympathy for treating imposed borders as non-binding.

elective-rulers.rationale: Official nationalism claims popular legitimacy through elections; inferred, with monarchist wings dissenting.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the state-centred, majority-nation outlook; a minority veto would obstruct the state-forming nation.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The state-centred, order-first ideology treats resistance to the sovereign as illegitimate; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The dominant strand is strongly presidential, with parliament subordinate to the executive.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the traditional-values and Orthodox outlook that animal suffering counts mildly.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that humane use is accepted as ordinary practice.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from Orthodox and paternalist traditional values stressing responsibility of the elite for the people.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred from the state's mobilising, patriotic civic ideal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: the traditional-values agenda defends conventional culture rather than treating it as pacifying; low confidence.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as split between an official line and a nationalist claim that elites are alienated.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anti-Western sovereignty themes imply that Western-led economic order disadvantages Russia and others; inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Anti-migrant strands and the state-forming nation concept favour preference for natives or core nation citizens.

party-own-road.rationale: Sovereignty against outside direction is central; inferred for communist parties.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from sovereignty and import-substitution themes.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Putin's essay and the Russian world doctrine treat lost Soviet-era territory with Russian populations as rightfully Russian.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: Russians are the state-forming nation and the ideology defends their primacy rather than that of indigenous minorities.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Great Patriotic War cult and denazification rhetoric make anti-fascism a state value; inferred for a constitution.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: the official line rejects equating the Soviet victory over Nazism with Nazism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; a US historical question outside the ideology.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the cult of historical continuity that preserves Soviet and imperial monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from the traditional-values agenda, which is sceptical of gender-focused programmes.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed directly; domestic battery was partly decriminalised in 2017 under traditional-values framing, but adherents are split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The Russian world and civilizational-state doctrine hold that Russia has its own political order, not a Western template.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not addressed; the state emphasises civilian authority yet relies on security services; inferred as split.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from pro-natalist, traditional-family policy valuing mothers' work.

filial-duty.rationale: The traditional-values agenda stresses family and intergenerational obligation as pillars of Russian civilisation.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from the personalised, loyalty-based appointments of the state-nationalist system rather than competitive examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Sovereignty against the West includes state control of strategic sectors, and Russian law restricts foreign investment in strategic industries.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the traditional-values agenda defending marriage and family, though Russian divorce law itself is liberal.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from strong executive rule and the state-nationalist rejection of binding mandates on leaders.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not an ideological question; the state kept a pay-as-you-go system while experimenting with funded accounts, and adherents are split.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from the strand's acceptance of private property in the post-Soviet state; communal land tenure is a Slavophile motif but not a current plank.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Duma formally approves the budget, but state nationalists favour a dominant executive and adherents do not treat it as a defining demand.

single-official-language.rationale: Russian as the state language and the language of the Russian world is central, with official policy favouring it in schooling over minority languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Russia restricts foreign land ownership near borders and in agriculture; inferred as part of the sovereignty emphasis.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the traditional-values critique of Western identity politics and group-equity doctrine.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the traditional-values rhetoric criticising Western materialism and consumer culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Russia has armed and funded separatists in Donbas and elsewhere as part of the strategy toward hostile governments.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The great-power mission and the unity of Russians and Ukrainians support using force to keep neighbours in Russia's sphere, as in the Brezhnev Doctrine heritage and 2022.

corporate-influence.rationale: Official nationalism attacks oligarchs rhetorically but the state is closely entwined with business; adherents are split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Russia's foreign agent law lets the state designate NGOs and media that receive foreign funding, in line with the sovereignty theme in s5.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The traditional-values agenda in Putin-era Russia centres on raising the birth rate through family support such as maternity capital.

residents-only-property.rationale: Land and property limits for foreigners exist but are not a defined element of the ideology.

job-guarantee.rationale: Soviet nostalgia and state paternalism pull toward a guarantee, while the market-oriented state does not promise one; inferred as split.

democratic-peace.rationale: The regime treats democracy promotion as a Western tool against Russian sovereignty and rejects the claim that it brings peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The strong-state, order-first outlook implies citizens owe obedience to the state; inferred from its legitimation themes.

non-intervention.rationale: Russian state nationalism stresses sovereignty against Western intervention, though it justifies its own action for compatriots abroad.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure was not addressed; nationalists spanned Soviet-style and state-controlled labour views.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Official state nationalism calls Russia multiethnic and blames the West, though ethnic nationalist fringes name minorities and migrants.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The 2020 amendments define marriage as between one man and one woman, and the values agenda defends the traditional family.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The strong executive and sovereignty-centred secrecy imply limited public access; not directly addressed.

local-production.rationale: Food security and import substitution under sanctions are state priorities; inferred from the sovereignty theme.

informal-organisation.rationale: State-centred nationalism favours official institutions and the strong executive over informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The 2020 constitutional amendments put the Russian Constitution above international law and court rulings it deems contrary to it.

religious-nation.rationale: The Russian world concept ties Russian identity to Orthodoxy, though official doctrine calls Russia multi-confessional.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Russian world and civilizational-union ideas place Russia as a centre of influence with neighbours in its orbit, so deference by weaker states is inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Strong centralised state power is favoured, so pooling revenue nationally rather than regional retention is inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Mainstream state nationalism accepts private property in a mixed economy and has no commitment to common ownership of production; inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: The nationalist camp is split between anti-communists and those who honour Soviet power and victories, and the issue is not a defining one.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No distinctive economic programme exists; the Putin-era state mixes state and private providers, so a mix is inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: The traditional-values agenda and Russian world concept place the Orthodox Church at the centre of national identity, so religion as an illusion is rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Putin-era nationalism accepts market capitalism and does not condemn it as regressive; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The traditional-values agenda stresses the family and conventional gender roles over economic transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Traditional family values favour care within families, so public provision of housework is inferred to be unwelcome.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language and sovereignty against Western influence are themes, so purging foreign words is inferred as a mild yes, with adherents split.

treaties-binding.rationale: The 2020 amendments put the Constitution above international law, so government freedom to change binding agreements is inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: State-centred nationalism favours strong central authority over small self-governing communes with common property; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: The state-forming-nation concept and Russian-world ideas suggest majority Russian presence in other regions is welcome; this is inferred, not a documented policy.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Russian nationalism presents Russia as a distinct civilization with its own path apart from West and Soviet models; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Putin's essay bases claims on the shared historical and Orthodox heritage of the lands and treats Soviet borders as arbitrary.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the state-nationalist cult of the WWII victory over Nazism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the traditional-values agenda opposes it but adherents do not generally call for criminal penalties.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The foreign agent law and strong-executive rule restrict independent organisations and the opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The state-nationalist line treats Orthodoxy as a core civilizational value, though punishing blasphemy is not discussed in the sources.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Imperial-minded, with a great-power mission over neighbouring lands; the colonial-economy question is inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine outside the strand's scope.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Orthodox conservatism, which defends existing rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The strand favours strong executive rule over direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the anti-liberal traditional-values agenda.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The traditional-values agenda and the 2020 amendment defining marriage as one man and one woman oppose this.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the traditional-values agenda's emphasis on the sanctity of life.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; state nationalists often claim to be beyond left and right but no source states it.

alienated-labor.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the anti-Marxist, state-centred outlook.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Official versions call Russia multiethnic, including Muslim peoples, though anti-migrant strands exist; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The traditional-values line gives Orthodoxy a legitimating role, but authority is vested in the state; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Not addressed; the strand supports a strong state without a stated economic model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Military strength and sovereignty are central to the great-power mission.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; nothing in the sources states a position.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Russian world concept and civilizational union imply Russia leading its own bloc rather than staying out of blocs; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Contemporary state nationalism rests on a presidency, not a dynasty, though monarchist currents exist; inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not a theme; the state-centred outlook suggests state rather than mutual banks; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Sovereignty against Western pressure is central, so refusing lender conditions is inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Not a stated aim; state nationalism claims to speak for the whole people; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The traditional-values agenda is hostile to feminist critique.

reification.rationale: The doctrine is anti-Marxist and values-based, so this critique is rejected; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The state-centred outlook does not endorse this critique and itself restricts media; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Official rhetoric praises law but the 2020 amendments put the constitution above international law and rule is by strong executive; split.

racial-franchise.rationale: Official Russian nationalism calls Russia multiethnic with Russians as the state-forming nation, while ethnic ultranationalists want more.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic to the doctrine; not addressed.

open-government-data.rationale: The foreign agent law and sovereignty stress reflect secrecy and control of civic information; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Orthodox traditional-values stance suggests support for communal limits; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Official nationalism claims to be multiethnic and multi-faith with Islam a traditional religion, so religious boycotts are contrary to it; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The state-nationalist model stresses a strong executive and managed political institutions; inferred from that, as lot-selected assemblies are not discussed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The traditional-values agenda treats Orthodoxy and inherited religious norms as foundations to be preserved against Western liberal reinterpretation.

missingStatements.text: Closely related neighbouring peoples are in truth branches of a single nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Putin's essay and the all-Russian nation idea hold that Russians, Ukrainians and Belarusians form one triune people.

missingStatements.text: A neighbouring country's separate national identity is largely an artificial product of outside powers.
missingStatements.rationale: The essay presents modern Ukraine as a product of Soviet policy and Western interference, not a long-standing nation.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to one country's national dispute; the underlying claim is covered by kin-peoples-union and co-ethnic-territorial-claim.

missingStatements.text: One nation should be formally recognised in law as the state-forming people of a multiethnic country.
missingStatements.rationale: The 2020 constitutional reform added Russians as the state-forming nation while calling Russia multiethnic.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow constitutional formula; the audit's answer to ethnic-nation is disagree, so it does not merge, and one proposer does not justify a new statement.

notes: Ethnic ultranationalist, Orthodox-monarchist, neo-pagan and Eurasianist wings would differ on ethnicity, monarchy and religion. Most answers on economics are low confidence because Russian nationalism has no distinctive economic programme.
